$comment: Advisories the npm-audit gate tolerates because no fixed version EXISTS.
This is not a way to defer work you could do today — an entry is only
legitimate when upgrading is impossible, and it must carry the reason,
the reachability assessment, and a review date. `scripts/audit-gate.mjs`
fails the build on an expired entry, and on an entry that no longer
matches anything (so a fix upstream forces the entry out rather than
leaving a permanent hole).
The gate itself is unchanged: still moderate+ on production deps.
2026-09-24: the two image-size entries were removed because image-size@2.0.3
shipped and both advisories (GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr, GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq) were
amended the same day to record it as the first patched version. The exemptions
rested on 'no patched release exists', which stopped being true — and the gate
failed them as STALE within the hour, which is the mechanism working.
NOTE: the tree still resolves image-size@1.2.1 via pptxgenjs@4.0.1, and npm
audit now reports it clean. Upgrading is a SEPARATE decision: image-size v2
changed the module's public shape (object, not a callable), which is why the
removed entries carried a doNotOverride warning. That warning is preserved in
git history and in tests/unit/pptx-image-size-unreachable.test.ts, which is
KEPT — it guards the claim that pptxgenjs never loads image-size at all, and
that property is worth holding whether or not an advisory is open.
2026-09-29: the tiptap entry below is a DIFFERENT KIND of exemption from the
image-size ones, and the difference matters. Those said 'no patched release
exists'. This one says 'the patched release exists AND WE ARE ON IT' — the
advisory's affected range simply predates the backport and was never amended.
It is the image-size situation caught one step earlier: before the advisory
metadata catches up rather than after. The same STALE mechanism will force it
out when the range is corrected upstream.
2026-10-06: the sprintf-js entry below is the classic kind: NO patched release
exists (the advisory covers every version through 1.1.3, the latest). Its only
production copy comes in through mammoth's command-line wrapper, which this app
never runs. The same day source-map-js went to 1.2.2, its patched release, so
that advisory needed no entry.

allow.title: Tiptap: mergeAttributes() turns an own __proto__ key into inherited executable DOM attributes
allow.reason: THE ADVISORY RANGE IS OVER-BROAD — it does not record the 2.x backport. Affected range is '>=2.0.0-alpha.0 <3.30.4'. tiptap fixed this in 3.30.4 (published 2026-08-26) and then BACKPORTED the identical fix to the 2.x line in 2.27.3 (published 2026-09-04, nine days LATER). The advisory's upper bound was never amended, so `npm audit` reports 2.27.3 as affected when it carries the fix. This is NOT 'no fixed version exists'. The fixed version exists and the tree is on it. Recorded plainly because the gate's refusal message asks for genuinely-unfixable, and this is a stale-metadata exemption instead.
allow.verification: Read: `mergeAttributes` in @tiptap/core@2.27.3 contains the guard — `if (key === '__proto__') Object.defineProperty(merged, key, {...})` — in BOTH the cjs and esm builds, character-for-character the same logic as the patched 3.31.3. Executed: the advisory's own attack shape (an own __proto__ key from JSON.parse) through the real 2.27.3 mergeAttributes leaves Object.prototype untouched and lands __proto__ as an own property. A naive merge of the same payload DOES pollute, which is the positive control proving the test can tell the two apart. Held: tests/guards/tiptap-proto-merge-is-fixed.test.ts runs that attack against EVERY @tiptap/core in the tree on every CI run, and fails if any copy falls below the 2.27.3 backport floor. Mutation-proved by disarming the guard in the @tldraw/editor copy — one named test went red.
allow.reachability: Two layers, and the second is the one that will change. 1. The code is not vulnerable — see verification above. That holds regardless of how we use it. 2. Exposure today is nil anyway: tldraw has ZERO import sites in src/ (the dependency is added ahead of the #2960 shape layer). When Phase 2 wires it up, tldraw's rich-text shapes become reachable by tenant users, so layer 2 stops being a mitigation — which is precisely why layer 1 is held by an executing guard rather than a note.
allow.upgradePlan: tldraw 3.x declares `@tiptap/* ^2.9.1` and cannot reach the 3.x line, so the route off 2.x is a tldraw major, not a tiptap bump. Forcing tiptap 3 under tldraw 3 via `overrides` was TESTED and rejected: it installs, clears the audit and passes a production build, then silently breaks the SECOND rich-text edit session — ProseMirror never remounts and keystrokes are discarded with no error. Evidence on #2960. The real route is tldraw 4.x/5.x, which ships tiptap 3.31.3 — gated on a commercial licence, because 4.0.0 onwards bans production use without a key (#2958). Revisit when that licence question is answered. Expected end state: this entry goes STALE on its own when the advisory range is amended to record 2.27.3, and the gate then forces it out.

allow.title: sprintf-js vulnerable to denial of service through unbounded precision specifiers
allow.reason: NO FIXED VERSION EXISTS. The advisory covers sprintf-js through 1.1.3, which is the latest release; there is nothing to upgrade to. The production tree's only copy is sprintf-js@1.0.3, pulled in as mammoth@1.13.0 -> argparse@1.0.10 -> sprintf-js. mammoth@1.13.0 is the latest mammoth and still declares `argparse: ~1.0.3`, so it cannot be moved by a bump either.
allow.verification: Traced on 2026-10-06 with `npm ls sprintf-js --omit=dev` (one path, through mammoth's argparse) and by reading the installed sources. In mammoth@1.13.0, `argparse` is required ONLY by `bin/mammoth`, the command-line wrapper; nothing under `lib/` (the library entry `main: ./lib/index.js`) requires it. In argparse@1.0.10, `sprintf` is called only from `argument_parser.js` and `help/formatter.js`, on argparse's own constant format strings (usage and help text), never on a caller-supplied format.
allow.reachability: Not reachable. The advisory needs an attacker-controlled FORMAT STRING. The app imports mammoth only as a library (`src/app-layer/integrations/providers/sharepoint/docx.ts`, `import mammoth from 'mammoth'`, resolving to lib/index.js) and never executes mammoth's CLI, which is the only code that loads argparse and so sprintf-js. Even inside the CLI, argparse formats its own help strings, not input. Document content converted by mammoth never reaches sprintf.
allow.upgradePlan: The entry leaves on either of two events, and the gate forces it out as STALE when one happens: sprintf-js ships a patched release and the advisory records it, or mammoth moves to argparse 2.x, which has no sprintf-js dependency. Overriding argparse to 2.x under mammoth was considered and not done: argparse 2 changed its API, so it would break mammoth's CLI to silence an advisory that the library path never touches. Revisit at reviewBy.
